notable_claims: Access to computing and information resources is a right, not a privilege.
Constitutional freedom of speech applies to citizens of electronic communities.
Educational institutions have a responsibility to provide legally acquired computer resources when they are integral to participation in the electronic community.
organizations: U.S. Congress Office of Technology Assessment
classification.summary: A draft document by EDUCOM proposing a framework of rights and responsibilities for individuals and institutions in the electronic educational community. It argues that access to computing resources is a right and emphasizes the balance between individual privacy, freedom of speech, and institutional security. The project aimed to extend traditional academic values into the context of information technology.
classification.title: Bill of Rights and Responsibilities for Electronic Learners
